title: Delete: the set_null walk's clear of a readonly lookup is stripped by the read-only rule, so rows keep the deleted record's id
body:
repo:hotcrm#1 · huangyiirene · session_01J8VVAnPkgK6CWrJa6t7Fk5

Found by the hotcrm lane's probe for hotcrm#2618 (report: hotcrm#2618 comment 6952320824) on @objectstack 18.5.0, local SQLite. Read in code on objectstack `main` fc5913e117.

## What happens

A lookup `crm_time_entry.crm_billing_milestone` declared `readonly: true` (default `deleteBehavior`, so `set_null`). An admin deletes the referenced `crm_billing_milestone` row: the delete answers 200, and the time entries still hold the deleted row's id. The server logs `Field 'crm_billing_milestone' on 'crm_time_entry' is read-only: the caller-supplied value was DROPPED and the update is being COMMITTED WITHOUT IT`. Discriminator: the same delete with the lookup **not** readonly clears it to null.

## Why, in code

- `packages/objectql/src/engine-cascade-planning.ts` ~1145–1183: the walk writes the clear with `this.update(childName, { id: depId, [fieldName]: null }, { context: referentialCtx })`, where `referentialCtx` is the caller's context plus `__referentialFieldClear: true`. It is not `isSystem`.
- `packages/objectql/src/validation/rule-validator.ts`: the read-only strip runs on `!context.isSystem` (doc ~2054, message `readonlyStripWarning` ~2790). Nothing in the strip reads `__referentialFieldClear` (grep: the marker is read only in `engine-middleware-and-context.ts` and `engine-master-detail-related.ts`).

So the engine's own referential cleanup is treated as a forged caller write and dropped.

## Consequence

A dangling id survives every delete of a referenced row whenever the lookup is readonly, which is the normal shape for a stamp a system writes (here: "billed on" a plan step). The row then looks linked forever: in hotcrm's design, entries billed on a deleted step look billed and are never billed again. Not cross-package specific.

## Asked

The referential clear written by the delete walk passes the read-only strip (it is the engine's write, not the caller's). Pin it with a test: readonly lookup, delete the target, the reference reads null.

## Done when

Deleting a record clears every `set_null` reference to it, readonly or not, and no read-only DROPPED line is logged for that clear.
